# Tools referenced by this skill

- [carbontracker](https://github.com/lfwa/carbontracker) - carbontracker tracks and predicts the energy consumption and carbon footprint of training deep learning models
- [CodeCarbon](https://codecarbon.io/) - CodeCarbon is a software package that integrates into Python codebase and estimates the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2) produced by the cloud or personal computing resources used to execute the code
- [covr](https://covr.r-lib.org/) - covr is an R package for measuring test coverage of R code, reporting which lines and functions are exercised by a test suite and integrating with continuous integration services to track coverage over time.
- [Dependabot](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core) - Generate automated pull requests updating dependencies for projects
- [Ecograder](https://ecograder.com/) - Evaluates website sustainability based on design and operational efficiency
- [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) - GitHub's infrastructure for continuous integration, deployment and delivery
- [GitLab CI/CD](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/topics/build_your_application.html) - GitLab's infrastructure for continuous integration, deployment and delivery
- [Green Algorithms](https://www.green-algorithms.org/) - An online tool to estimate the carbon footprint of computational tasks using a web calculator
- [Greenspector Studio](https://greenspector.com/en/home/) - Greenspector is a tool that measures energy usage and resource efficiency in web and mobile applications
- [lintr](https://lintr.r-lib.org/) - lintr is a static analysis tool for R code that checks for style errors, syntax errors, and possible semantic issues, helping to enforce consistent coding standards across R projects.
- [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip/) - pip is the package installer for Python. It allows you to install and manage additional libraries and dependencies that are not part of the Python standard library.
- [pip-tools](https://pip-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) - pip-tools is a set of command-line tools to help keep Python package dependencies up to date and pinned reproducibly via requirements.in and requirements.txt files.
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/) - Python packaging and dependency management tool
- [pytest-cov](https://pytest-cov.readthedocs.io/) - pytest-cov is a pytest plugin that produces coverage reports for Python code, integrating with the coverage.py library to show which lines are exercised by tests.
- [Renovatebot](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) - Automates dependency updates, multi-platform and multi-language.
- [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/index.html) - renv is an R package that helps you create reproducible environments for your R projects - use renv to make your R projects more isolated, portable and reproducible
- [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) - An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter written in Rust
- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) - Semantic versioning (SemVer) is a widely-adopted version scheme that encodes a version of a project by a three-part version number (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), an optional pre-release tag, and an optional build meta tag.
- [SonarQube](https://www.sonarcatalog.com/products/sonarqube/) - Continuous inspection of code quality to perform automatic reviews for static analysis of code
- [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) - uv is an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
- [venv](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html) - venv is a Python module for creating lightweight “virtual environments”, each with their own independent set of Python packages installed in their site directories
